scope: All verified overall top-three winners in ShellHacks 2022, 2023 and 2024, including the separate 2022 virtual podium.
method: Award text verified on each primary Devpost project page under the named ShellHacks event. Project capabilities are authors' descriptions, not independently tested. No winning inference is made from submission alone.

flag_codebook.yes: Explicitly described current feature or component.
flag_codebook.not_evidenced: Not described as current; not proof of absence.
flag_codebook.ai_ml: Named AI/ML model or explicit machine-learning implementation; computer vision or sentiment analysis alone may remain ambiguous.
flag_codebook.external_api_service: External API, external data integration, or hosted cloud service; local libraries alone do not qualify.
flag_codebook.accessibility_inclusion: Explicit disability access or support for an underserved population; ordinary usability alone does not qualify.
flag_codebook.social_benefit: Education, health, food access, civic or environmental goal; generic productivity alone does not qualify.
flag_codebook.visual_demo_interface: Described visual UI, interactive visualization, or physical demonstrator; not an assessment of design quality.
flag_codebook.hardware: Specialized sensor/headset/physical prototype integral to workflow; ordinary laptop/phone alone does not qualify.

editions.winner_count_note: 24 winner badges on gallery page 1 and 7 on page 2; later pages not audited, so use as observed count/minimum, not an established census.
editions.note: Separate First/Second/Third Place and First/Second/Third Place (Virtual) categories.

editions.winner_count_note: 24 winner badges on gallery page 1 and 14 on page 2; later pages not audited, so use as observed count/minimum, not an established census.
editions.note: Project pages explicitly identify Second Place Overall and Third Place Overall even though the overview prominently lists Best Overall.

editions.winner_count_note: 24 winner badges on gallery page 1 and 17 on page 2; later pages not audited, so use as observed count/minimum, not an established census.
editions.note: Overview location field says Online while overall prize descriptions say in-person projects; do not infer event format from that field.

projects.name: The Tilter
projects.target_problem: A concrete control-engineering challenge: keep a golf ball balanced on a moving platform.
projects.workflow: Phone camera tracks the ball; Python PID control sends serial commands to Arduino servos.

evidence.ai_ml: Computer-vision tracking is described, but no learned model is specified.
evidence.visual_demo_interface: Working ball-balancing platform and video link.
evidence.hardware: Arduino, servo motors and cardboard platform.

projects.limitations: Engineering demonstrator; no explicit civic/health/education beneficiary is claimed. Future joystick game is a proposal.

projects.name: Pegasus
projects.target_problem: Help organizations search securities data and identify source-code vulnerabilities.
projects.workflow: Upload CSV data for indexed queries or source code for rule-based vulnerability scanning and alerts.

evidence.external_api_service: AWS Lambda/API Gateway backend and IPFS network.
evidence.visual_demo_interface: React frontend accepts uploads and presents vulnerability results.

projects.limitations: Authors explicitly linked ideation to Schonfeld and MITRE challenges. Scanning is custom regex-based; do not relabel it ML.

projects.name: Saberfy
projects.target_problem: Beat Saber players lack maps for some preferred songs; manual creation takes time.
projects.workflow: Supply a Spotify song link; Python translates song characteristics into importable Beat Saber map files with difficulty variants.

evidence.external_api_service: Spotify Web API and other APIs provide song data.
evidence.visual_demo_interface: Website/graphics and playable map output described.

projects.limitations: A team member says the direct website-to-server integration was unfinished. VR game output does not establish custom hardware development.

projects.name: DAOchow
projects.target_problem: Food-insecure residents need access to community fridges and transparent funding.
projects.workflow: A decentralized web app connects users to food access and manages funds through a DAO.

evidence.ai_ml: Authors explicitly report implementing TensorFlow for an ML model.
evidence.external_api_service: Azure hosting and API calls described.
evidence.accessibility_inclusion: Targets food-insecure and financially constrained users.
evidence.visual_demo_interface: Map, proposals, tasks and profile screens.

projects.limitations: ML task is unspecified. USDA-based placement of new fridges is future work, not a demonstrated function.

projects.name: AlgoSaurus
projects.target_problem: Beginning programmers struggle to understand sorting algorithms.
projects.workflow: Choose an algorithm, observe animated sorting, and adjust chart size or speed while reading explanations.

evidence.external_api_service: Firebase appears in Built With and a web.app deployment is linked.
evidence.visual_demo_interface: Animated charts with adjustable speed and bar count.

projects.limitations: Authentication, tutoring and chat are proposed future additions. Ordinary beginner education is not automatically disability/inclusion evidence.

projects.name: Ping Path
projects.target_problem: People with visual impairments need safer, more independent navigation around obstacles and destinations.
projects.workflow: LiDAR and ML interpret surroundings; spatial audio guides users, with shared maps and voice interactions.

evidence.accessibility_inclusion: Visually impaired target users, Siri shortcuts and VoiceOver testing.
evidence.visual_demo_interface: App interface, beta link and video.

projects.limitations: Authors report conversations with visually impaired users; efficacy not independently validated. Non-LiDAR support is inconsistently described as current versus after the hackathon.

projects.name: Chess 10
projects.target_problem: Give chess players a new strategic experience through altered rules and multiple participants.
projects.workflow: Play a 3D chess variant extending en passant mechanics to most pieces.

evidence.visual_demo_interface: 3D board, models, animated background and React UI; demo and repository links.

projects.limitations: No AI, social-impact or API integration is reported. New mechanics and implementation are described; originality is not independently assessed.

projects.name: IntelliSchedule
projects.target_problem: College students waste time switching between course selection and professor reviews.
projects.workflow: Chrome extension places ratings, difficulty, return-interest scores and review summaries alongside FIU course choices.

evidence.ai_ml: Sentiment analysis described without model details; chatbot is future work.
evidence.external_api_service: Rate My Professors and FIU course data integrated.
evidence.visual_demo_interface: Browser extension displays ratings beside class options.

projects.limitations: No sponsor rank stated on award label. AI classification remains ambiguous; do not count proposed chatbot as implemented.

projects.name: MedVoyage
projects.target_problem: Offer users a guided route from symptom questions to a preliminary diagnostic suggestion.
projects.workflow: A website walks users through a JavaScript binary decision tree.

evidence.visual_demo_interface: Website with parallax design and linked live page.

projects.limitations: A binary decision tree is not necessarily trained ML. Accuracy and safety claims are unvalidated; support for different screen sizes is explicitly future work.

projects.name: Epileptic Seizure Prevention and Early Response (ESPER)
projects.target_problem: Reduce abrupt brightness changes in web video for people with epilepsy.
projects.workflow: A browser extension measures frame luminosity, applies CSS brightness adjustments, and uploads video characteristics to an analytical dashboard.

evidence.ai_ml: Application of data to ML/AI is listed as next work.
evidence.external_api_service: YouTube API, Snowflake database and cloud hosting.
evidence.social_benefit: Intended reduction of exposure to seizure-triggering flashes.

projects.limitations: No clinical outcome is demonstrated. Sponsor label has no rank.

projects.name: ARSL - Augmented Reality Sign Language
projects.target_problem: Make ASL alphabet learning interactive and connected to surrounding objects.
projects.workflow: Quest passthrough identifies objects; hand tracking and a vibrating glove guide the learner through spelling.

evidence.ai_ml: Image/pose recognition models and PyTorch described.
evidence.hardware: Quest headset plus functional vibrating glove.

projects.limitations: Object/gesture recognition accuracy needs improvement; whole-word mode is future work. Sponsor ranks unspecified.

projects.name: Diffusion Earth
projects.target_problem: Let learners explore environments beyond static images.
projects.workflow: Start with an image, prompt or address; generate depth/point clouds and synthesize new views as the user moves.

evidence.ai_ml: Diffusion generation, depth estimation and inpainting models.
evidence.external_api_service: Google Maps Street View imagery and hosted GPUs.
evidence.social_benefit: Educational exploration is the stated motivation.
evidence.visual_demo_interface: Navigable environment via WASD or onscreen buttons.

projects.limitations: Authors report reducing frame generation from about 120 seconds to 10–15 seconds; this is self-reported. Urban planning/conservation applications are future proposals.

interpretation_notes: The sampled projects are overall winners, not a random sample of all entrants or all sponsor winners. Winner-only feature prevalence cannot estimate winning probability or causation.
Visual interface/demonstrator evidence is universal in these 12 sampled descriptions; this is not proof that judges rewarded presentation quality.
The Tilter, Saberfy and Chess 10 show that an explicit social-impact narrative is not universal among overall winners.
ESPER explicitly defers AI/ML to future work, while Chess 10 describes a graphics/game-logic stack without AI. AI is not established as necessary to win.
Do not equate Devpost registered-participant totals with in-person attendance; do not sum prize-category winner counts as unique projects.
Source summaries intentionally omit participant names and personal details. Each evidence object refers to its containing project URL.
